answer: Mailed-address checks stop Sybils in three steps. First, a newcomer posts a $30 bond and a postal address; the registry mails a one-time code: one key, one mailbox. Second, the code must be redeemed in 30 days, one bridge, one traveler at a time; peers re-mail one address in ten with a hidden mark. Third, failure burns the bond, bans the key 90 days, and blacklists the address. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 addresses plus $30,000 in bonds and $5,000 postage, all lost when caught. Trust grows like an oasis fed by real mail; a jade seal means little until the letter proves the house.
